questions.stem: The VEDIC AGE in ancient India — marked by composition of the Vedas — lasted approximately:
questions.explanation: VEDIC AGE (~1500 BCE - 600 BCE): divided into EARLY VEDIC (RIGVEDIC, ~1500-1000 BCE) + LATER VEDIC (~1000-600 BCE). Followed the decline of the HARAPPAN (INDUS VALLEY) civilisation. Sources: the 4 VEDAS — our primary knowledge. EARLY VEDIC — lived in 'SAPTA SINDHAVA' (land of seven rivers — Punjab region). Semi-nomadic, pastoral, cattle-rearing. Tribal polity (GANA). Worshipped nature gods — INDRA (god of war, storm), AGNI (fire), VARUNA (cosmic order), SURYA, USHA, etc. COMPOSED RIGVEDA (10 mandalas, 1028 hymns). LATER VEDIC — expanded eastward from Punjab to Ganga-Yamuna doab + onwards. Settled agriculture, iron tools (PGW culture = Painted Grey Ware). Rise of kingdoms (JANAPADAS). Composed SAMA-, YAJUR-, ATHARVA-VEDAS + BRAHMANAS + ARANYAKAS + UPANISHADS. Rise of VARNA system (4-fold caste: Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya, Shudra) based on birth. Period ended with the rise of MAHAJANAPADAS (600 BCE onwards — 16 great kingdoms) + heterodox religions (Buddhism + Jainism). Early Vedic 1500-1000 BCE; Later Vedic 1000-600 BCE.

questions.stem: The OLDEST and MOST IMPORTANT Veda is:
questions.explanation: THE FOUR VEDAS (meaning 'KNOWLEDGE' in Sanskrit): (1) RIG VEDA (Rigveda, ~1500-1200 BCE) — OLDEST, most important. 10 MANDALAS (books), 1028 SUKTAS (hymns), ~10,600 verses. Mandalas 2-7 are the OLDEST 'Family Mandalas'. Famous hymns: GAYATRI MANTRA (3rd mandala, to Savitri), PURUSHA SUKTA (10th, on the creation + 4 varnas). Dedicated to gods — Agni (most hymns), Indra (2nd most). (2) SAMA VEDA ('Veda of Melodies/Chants') — musical rendering of Rig Veda verses for ritual chanting; considered the origin of INDIAN CLASSICAL MUSIC. (3) YAJUR VEDA ('Veda of Sacrificial Formulas') — prose + verse formulae for yajnas (sacrifices). Two recensions: Krishna (Taittiriya etc.) + Shukla (Vajasaneyi/Madhyandina). (4) ATHARVA VEDA ('Veda of Atharvan, a Priest') — LATEST, contains spells, charms, folk practices, medicine (Ayurveda origins), daily life issues. Considered by orthodox Brahmins as 'less holy' initially; later accepted. Each Veda has 4 divisions: SAMHITAS (mantras), BRAHMANAS (ritual commentary), ARANYAKAS ('forest books', mystical), UPANISHADS (philosophical, 'Vedanta — end of Vedas'). UPANISHADS (~108; 10-13 principal ones) are the philosophical core. 10 mandalas / books, 1028 hymns / suktas.

questions.stem: Which river is mentioned MOST frequently in the RIGVEDA, and is considered the 'MOTHER' of Vedic culture?
questions.explanation: RIGVEDIC RIVERS — the Rig Veda mentions SAPTA SINDHAVA ('SEVEN RIVERS' — seven sacred rivers): Sindhu (Indus), Jhelum (Vitasta), Chenab (Asikni), Ravi (Parushni), Beas (Vipasa), Sutlej (Shutudri), and SARASVATI. SARASVATI is mentioned 72 TIMES in the Rigveda — FAR MORE than any other river — regarded as the 'MOTHER OF WATERS' + 'best of rivers'. Today SARASVATI is DRIED UP — identified with the GHAGGAR-HAKRA palaeo-channel (which flowed through NW India + Pakistan). GANGA is mentioned only ONCE in the Rigveda; YAMUNA thrice — suggesting Vedic society was centred in Punjab, with minimal early contact with eastern Ganga valley. Rig Veda also mentions: Kubha (Kabul), Gomati, Krumu (Kurram), Suvastu (Swat). LATER VEDAS show eastward shift — more references to Yamuna, Ganga. MAHABHARATA confirms Saraswati's drying up ('Saraswati Vinasanam'). ISRO satellite imaging has mapped ancient Saraswati palaeo-channels. Today observed as a 'mythical' river — supposedly the hidden third river at PRAYAGRAJ (Triveni Sangam). mentioned 72 times, most of any river.

questions.stem: The VARNA system — the 4-fold classification of society — is first mentioned in which hymn of the Rig Veda?
questions.explanation: PURUSHA SUKTA (Rig Veda 10.90) — one of the latest Rigvedic hymns. Describes the COSMIC PURUSHA (primeval man) whose sacrifice by the gods produced the universe. The four VARNAS emerge from different parts of his body: BRAHMIN (priests + scholars) from his MOUTH; KSHATRIYA (warriors + rulers) from his ARMS; VAISHYA (merchants + cultivators) from his THIGHS; SHUDRA (labourers + service) from his FEET. Later fossilised into the rigid JATI (caste) system with thousands of sub-castes. Original Vedic varna may have been occupation-based + flexible; became HEREDITARY + RIGID in later Vedic times. NOTE: DALITS / 'UNTOUCHABLES' originally outside varna system ('Panchama' 5th varna in some texts — below Shudras). Abolished by Article 17 of Constitution. Other famous Rig Vedic hymns: GAYATRI MANTRA (3.62.10, to Savitri — most chanted mantra in Hinduism); NASADIYA SUKTA (10.129 — the 'creation hymn' with philosophical speculation about origins — 'Who knows whence creation arose?'). USHAS SUKTA — dawn goddess. Rig Veda, 10th Mandala, 90th Sukta.

questions.stem: The UPANISHADS — philosophical texts at the end of each Veda — are also called:
questions.explanation: UPANISHADS = 'VEDANTA' (from anta = 'end') — the concluding philosophical portions of each Veda. ~108 Upanishads traditionally accepted; 10-13 are considered 'PRINCIPAL UPANISHADS': Isha, Kena, Katha, Prashna, Mundaka, Mandukya, Taittiriya, Aitareya, Chandogya, Brihadaranyaka, Shvetashvatara, Kaushitaki, Maitri. Core ideas: BRAHMAN (ultimate reality), ATMAN (individual soul), their identity ('TAT TVAM ASI' — That Thou Art; 'AHAM BRAHMASMI' — I am Brahman); MOKSHA (liberation from cycle of birth-death); KARMA + SAMSARA. Rejected mechanical ritualism of earlier Vedic period in favour of inner knowledge. Shankaracharya (8th c. CE) expounded ADVAITA VEDANTA based on them. Translated by DARA SHIKOH (Mughal prince) in 1657 into Persian ('Sirr-i-Akbar'), introduced to Europe via Anquetil-Duperron's Latin translation — deeply influenced German philosopher Schopenhauer. OTHER HINDU TEXTS: PURANAS (mythological narratives — 18 Mahapuranas); SMRITIS (dharma codes — Manusmriti); EPICS (Ramayana, Mahabharata); AGAMAS + TANTRAS; 6 DARSHANAS (philosophical schools: Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Samkhya, Yoga, Mimamsa, Vedanta). 'End of the Vedas'.

questions.stem: In the EARLY VEDIC PERIOD, the political institution 'SABHA' was:

options.option_text: An assembly of selected nobles / elders

questions.explanation: EARLY VEDIC POLITICAL INSTITUTIONS: (1) SABHA — an assembly of nobles + elders, sometimes with women present ('SABHAVATI' — dignified lady of sabha). (2) SAMITI — general assembly of tribal members (sometimes translated 'folk assembly'); larger than sabha. Both are considered democratic-like checks on royal power. (3) VIDATHA — oldest, earliest folk-assembly; possibly for religious/social/distributive functions. (4) GANA — the tribal group/nation itself. Later they declined in importance as kingship became hereditary + bureaucratised. RAJAN (king) — elected initially by the tribe, later hereditary. Helped by PUROHITA (priest — chief advisor), SENANI (army chief), GRAMINI (village head). No standing army (warriors called up as needed). Tribes mentioned: BHARATAS, PURUS, YADUS, TURVASAS, ANUS, DRUHYUS (the 'PANCHA-JANA' — five tribes). Famous BATTLE OF TEN KINGS (Dasarajna Yuddha) — described in Rig Veda; won by Sudas, king of Bharata-Tritsu confederacy against 10 other tribes including Purus. BHARATA tribe gave India its name ('BHARATA-VARSHA'). possibly the upper chamber of Vedic assembly; women could attend.

questions.stem: The WRITING SCRIPT used in the Vedic Sanskrit literature (centuries LATER when Vedas were finally written down) is:

options.option_text: Devanagari (a descendant of Brahmi, developed around 7th-8th c. CE); oldest surviving scripts of Sanskrit: Brahmi → Gupta → Siddham → Devanagari

questions.explanation: Vedic Sanskrit was initially transmitted ORALLY for centuries — the famous ŚRUTI tradition ('that which is heard'). Oral memorisation with strict phonetic + grammatical rules preserved the Vedas UNCHANGED across generations. Writing in India: (1) INDUS SCRIPT (~2500 BCE, Harappan) — undeciphered, possibly not Indo-European. (2) BRAHMI SCRIPT (~3rd c. BCE, Ashokan edicts) — ancestor of most modern Indian scripts + Southeast Asian (Thai, Burmese, Khmer, Balinese). Deciphered by James Prinsep 1837. (3) KHAROSHTHI — used in NW India/Pakistan (~3rd c. BCE - 3rd c. CE); right-to-left. (4) GUPTA BRAHMI — Gupta-era development. (5) SIDDHAM (Siddhamatrika) — 7th c. CE — used for Buddhist texts in Japan (Shingon). (6) DEVANAGARI — evolved from Nagari (~7th-10th c. CE) — now used for Sanskrit, Hindi, Marathi, Nepali, Konkani, Maithili, Bodo, Dogri. Scripts of Indian languages: Bengali-Assamese, Gurmukhi (Punjabi), Gujarati, Odia, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, etc. — all descend from Brahmi. KEY: Vedic knowledge OLDER THAN WRITING — preserved orally for possibly 1000+ years.
